$comment: Everything about this repository that the shared pipeline needs and cannot detect. The pipeline lives in marius-patrik/DarkFactory and is pinned below; the workflows here are callers, not copies.

identity.description: Omnis — graph-native agentic operating system built on Linux and Nix, with OmnisOS, OmnisManager, OmnisAgent, OmnisControl, and one shared multidimensional graph.

upstream.$comment: The shared pipeline. `ref` is the pin: bump it to adopt a pipeline update, and the diff shows exactly what changed.

environment.$comment: Rust, TypeScript and the Python automation are all detected. The docs build is first-party, so it is declared.

release.$comment: pyproject.toml here carries only tooling configuration, so there is nothing for `python -m build` to produce and setuptools sees theme/ and notes/ as rival top-level packages. A release here is a tag and its notes, with no assets.

areas.$comment: Omnis's own domains. Declaration order is match order, so specific areas come before general ones.

term.description: OmnisControl shell, PTY, terminal/text projections and cell-grid compatibility

browser.description: OmnisControl web/navigation surfaces and browser protocol/native bindings

agents.description: OmnisAgent cognition plus Manager-provided model and external agent-harness bindings

ext.description: OmnisManager foreign capabilities, arbitrary bindings, MCP and protocol integration

data.description: Shared graph, OmnisAgent worldline/memory, artifacts, persistence and indexes

ui.description: OmnisControl graph desktop, 2D/3D projection, rendering, interaction and native surfaces

ci.description: GitHub Actions workflows, containers, runner scripts, repository automation

core.description: OmnisOS, OmnisManager, shared graph/protocol substrate, boot, generations and cross-component integration

license.$comment: Written from GitHub's canonical text, so it cannot drift from the wording it claims to be. NONE means deliberately not licensed for reuse, which is different from having forgotten to choose. Change it through a configuration issue.

$comment_required_checks: Written rather than defaulted: calling the pipeline as a reusable workflow prefixes every check with the caller's job name, so the unprefixed defaults would protect the branch against contexts nothing reports.
